podcast.title: Vancouver-Based Fierce Band (1986-1993)
podcast.body: Sons of Freedom was a "very fierce" band originating from Vancouver, active for a seven-year period from 1986 to 1993. "a very fierce band at a Vancouver, which existed from 1986 through to 1993."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Casby Award for Most Promising Group (1989)
podcast.body: The band won a Casby Award in 1989, being recognized as the most promising group. "They won a Casby Award for most promising group in 1989."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Juno Nomination (1990)
podcast.body: Following their Casby win, they received a Juno Award nomination in the same category the subsequent year. "and then they were nominated in the same June category the following year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rise in 1992
podcast.body: Sons of Freedom began their rise in 1992, becoming part of a significant wave of new Canadian artists. Their emergence contributed to the growing diversity and popularity of the Canadian music scene in the early 90s. "1992, Sons of Freedom, Boot Sauce, Lowest of the Low, More Hip, More Barodicad Ladies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.title: Major Label Association and Dropping (1993)
podcast.body: The band had an association with a major label, but they were dropped in 1993, leading to their breakup. "There was a dalliance with a major label, but when they were dropped in 1993, Sons of Freedom broke up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Reformation as Black Eye Buddha (1993)
podcast.body: After their breakup in 1993, the members of Sons of Freedom reformed under the new name Black Eye Buddha. "Sons of Freedom broke up and reformed under the name Black Eye Buddha."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: One-Off Reunion Show (2014)
podcast.body: The band had a reunion show in 2014, although it was explicitly stated to be a single, non-recurring event. "I should point out that there was a reunion show in 2014, but that was just a one-off thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early 1990s Prime Time Success
podcast.body: Sons of Freedom were among the Canadian bands that achieved "prime time" exposure in the early 1990s, reflecting the era's vibrant music scene. "The early 90s were pretty amazing with a long list of Canadian bands getting a shot at prime time. We had moist, the watchman, lowest of the low, sons of freedom, grapes of wrath, rhymes with orange, pure Gandarva's limb lifter."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members' Involvement in Two Precious
podcast.body: Three members of the band, all named Don (Don Harrison, Don Shorten, Don Bins), later joined forces with "Metal Queen" Lee Aaron in a group called Two Precious. "The three guys named Don from the band, Don Harrison, Don Shorten, Don Bins. They got together with Metal Queen Lee Aaron in a band called Two Precious."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Notable Contributors to Music
xref.body: Over the years, Jackalope's music featured contributions from a range of distinguished artists, including members of Sloan and Monster Magnet, Trent Reznor of Nine Inch Nails (who also co-produced), Alex Lifeson of Rush, and the three members named Don from Sons of Freedom. "Over the next few years, a number of really interesting artists contributed to Jackalope's music. The members of Sloan, the members of Monster Magnet, Trent Resner of Nine-H nails acted as a co-producer for a while. Alex Lifeson of Rush, and like I said, the three Don's from Sons of Freedom."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
